mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates economic weakness, leading to negative investor sentiment and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 2% over the previous six months signals strong economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% over the previous six months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a reduction in supply, leading to increased costs and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.1% in the same month, signals increased demand and lower borrowing costs, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 10% and FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable economic environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% in a month signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 5% in the previous month.
